new_statements.quote: [p.12] Der Akzent ist grundsätzlich der gleiche wie im Neupersischen. Auch andere Mundarten und nicht zuletzt das Neupersische schwanken in ihrer Betonung, insofern innerhalb eines Satzganzen die Endbetonung der Einzelwörter oft aufgehoben erscheint (Sandhi-Wirkung). [p.13] ... Im Chunsari tritt die Anfangsbetonung des den Satz beginnenden Wortes stark hervor; d.h. die erste Silbe des Satzes (außer vä, o „und”) erhält sehr oft einen kräftigen Akzent, der den Endakzent des Wortes überklingt ... Am Satzende liegt die andere große Tonstelle. [p.341] Der Akzent wird nur dort bezeichnet, wo er nicht auf der letzten Silbe liegt. [p.48] Der Plural wird durch Anhängen von betontem -ā (np. -hā) gebildet.
new_statements.translation: [p.12] The accent is fundamentally the same as in New Persian. Other dialects too, and not least New Persian, fluctuate in their stressing, in that within a sentence-whole the final stress of the individual words often appears suspended (sandhi effect). [p.13] ... In Chunsari the initial stressing of the word that begins the sentence stands out strongly; i.e. the first syllable of the sentence (except vä, o 'and') very often receives a strong accent which drowns out the word's final accent ... At the end of the sentence lies the other major stress position. [p.341] The accent is marked only where it does not lie on the last syllable. [p.48] The plural is formed by adding stressed -ā (NP -hā).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent as in New Persian: on the final syllable of the word (nominal inflections such as plural -ā take the stress); non-final accent is the marked case (Persian-type exceptions, e.g. certain clitics/particles and verbal prefixes, are implied by 'as in New Persian' but not itemised). In connected speech word-final stress is frequently overridden: the sentence-initial syllable often carries a strong accent and the sentence end is the other main prominence.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Eilers states (p. 11 fn. 1) that he could not record finer distinctions such as main vs secondary stress (Haupt- und Nebenton) or dynamic vs pitch accent; no secondary-stress rule given.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent 'as in New Persian' implies the Persian non-final cases; Eilers notes NP-style fluctuation (yekí ~ yéki, digarí ~ dígari); sentence-initial words take initial stress overriding Endakzent (except the conjunctions vä, o 'and'); Endbetonung often suspended sentence-internally (sandhi); glossary marks only non-final accents. Mann & Hadank 1926 add that the determinative suffix -ä is fully stressed while accusative -ä is at most half-stressed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level default is final (citation/lexical form, per glossary convention); Eilers explicitly separates this from sentence accent, where initial and final positions of the sentence attract prominence and word-final stress may be neutralised. Data: dictated narrative texts from one Khunsar-born informant (1940-41) plus 1974 field notes.
new_statements.identity_note: Eilers & Schapka 1976 describe the dialect of the town of Khunsar (Chunsar/Khvansar) as dictated by one native informant (Mehbud) in 1940-41, with Eilers' own 1974 notes from the Khunsar valley and neighbouring Vanešan (Vaneshani, treated as a close sister dialect; Glottolog files it with khun1255's western CPD neighbours). This is the same variety as Glottolog khun1255 / ISO kfm. Mann & Hadank 1926 'Khunsari' is likewise Khunsar town (Mann's 1903 texts).

sources.citation: Mann, Oskar & Karl Hadank. 1926. Kurdisch-persische Forschungen III/1: Die Mundarten von Khunsar, Mahallat, Natanz, Nayin, Samnan, Sivand und So-Kohrud. Berlin/Leipzig: de Gruyter.
sources.note: No dedicated accent section for Khunsari. Hadank's Einleitung (a) 'Vom Khunsari' and 'Zur Grammatik: A. Vom Nomen' remark only that the determinative suffix -a is spoken 'mit Volldruck' (fully stressed) whereas the colloquial accusative -a is at most half-stressed/post-tonic; Mann's texts carry stress marks (Druckakzent).
Nothing on stress; cites only Ethnologue/Glottolog/newspaper items.
